extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies, Non-Federal applicants, and NCPC staff involved in NEPA compliance for projects in the National Capital Region
extracted.subtask_short: NCPC NEPA compliance and CATEX rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance from the National Capital Planning Commission establishing NEPA process roles (Lead/Cooperating agencies), submission timing, Categorical Exclusion criteria, extraordinary circumstances, and specific NCPC categorical exclusions for projects within NCPC jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Document definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental Document means, as set forth in 40 CFR 1508.10, an Environmental Assessment, an Environmental Impact Statement, and for purposes of these regulations, a Categorical Exclusion determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the documents that satisfy NCPC's NEPA obligations; references CEQ definitions at 40 CFR 1508.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental Impact Statement or EIS means, as defined in 40 CFR 1508.11, a detailed written statement as required by 42 U.S.C. 4332(2)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard CEQ definition; EIS is the full, detailed NEPA analysis for actions with significant impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: FONSI means, as defined at 40 CFR 1508.13, a document prepared that briefly presents the reasons why an action will not have a significant effect and for which an EIS will not be prepared. It shall include the EA or a summary of it and shall note any other EAs or EISs related to it. If the EA is included in the FONSI, the FONSI need not repeat EA discussion but may include the EA by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing a FONSI, include or reference the EA and list related NEPA documents per 40 CFR 1501.7(a)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation definition and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigation means avoiding impacts by not taking an action or parts of an action; minimizing impacts by limiting degree or magnitude; rectifying impact by repairing/rehabilitating/restoring; reducing or eliminating impact over time by preservation and maintenance during life of action; compensating for impact by replacing or providing substitute resources/environments (40 CFR 1508.20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation can include avoidance, minimization, restoration, long-term maintenance, and compensation; consider all forms when addressing impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency designation for Federal Agency applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal Agency applicant shall serve as the Lead Agency and prepare an EA or an EIS for: (1) an application that requires Commission approval; and (2) an application for action on a master plan that includes future projects that require Commission approval, provided the applicant intends to submit individual projects within five years and intends to use the master plan EA/EIS to satisfy NEPA obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when Federal applicants must be Lead Agencies and when master-plan tiering is acceptable (five-year and NEPA-satisfaction conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC designation as Lead Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall serve as Lead Agency and prepare an EA or an EIS for: (1) an application submitted by a Non-Federal Agency that requires Commission approval; (2) an application submitted by a Non-Federal Agency for action on a master plan with the same five-year and NEPA-satisfaction conditions; and (3) an application for approval of land acquisitions under 40 U.S.C. 8731–8732.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when NCPC will act as Lead (non-federal applicants and certain land acquisition actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: act as Lead per 40 CFR 1501.5
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lead Agency must act as Lead Agency as defined in 40 CFR 1501.5 for the NEPA process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow CEQ procedural responsibilities and standards for Lead Agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: integrate other environmental and regulatory reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate other environmental reviews and other applicable regulatory requirements to include, without limitation, Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate NEPA with other statutory environmental reviews to avoid duplication and ensure all required compliance tasks are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: allow NCPC participation and consultation early
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow NCPC to participate as a Co-lead or Cooperating Agency, as appropriate, and consult with Commission staff as early as possible to obtain guidance on goals, objectives, standards, purpose, need, and alternatives for the NEPA analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement with NCPC staff is required to align NEPA scope and analysis with Commission expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: invite affected agencies as Cooperating Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite affected Federal, state, regional and local agencies to participate as a Cooperating Agency in the NEPA process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively identify and solicit cooperation from agencies with jurisdictional or special expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: consult early with affected agencies for guidance on NEPA scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult with the affected agencies as early as possible in the planning process to obtain guidance on the goals, objectives, standards, purpose, need, and alternatives for the NEPA analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early consultation helps define scope and reduces later disputes; same subject matter as (3) but emphasizes consultation with affected agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: work with Cooperating Agencies and stakeholders (information exchange & review opportunities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with Cooperating Agencies and stakeholders by (i) keeping them informed on project schedule and substantive matters; and (ii) allowing them reasonable time to review and comment on Public Scoping notices; technical reports; public materials (including responses to public comments); potential mitigation measures; the draft EA or EIS; and the draft FONSI or ROD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely materials and reasonable review periods for cooperating agencies and stakeholders on all key NEPA products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: prepare appropriate Environmental Document consistent with NEPA and CEQ regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the appropriate Environmental Document consistent with the applicant's NEPA regulations, the requirements of this part, and CEQ regulations. If the Lead Agency applies a Categorical Exclusion and NCPC as a Cooperating Agency does not have a corresponding CATEX, the Lead Agency shall prepare an EA to satisfy NCPC's NEPA requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the chosen NEPA instrument is acceptable to NCPC; when NCPC cannot apply the same CATEX, an EA must be prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: determine adverse impacts and limit on alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine in its Environmental Document whether an action will have an adverse environmental impact or would limit the choice of reasonable alternatives under 40 CFR 1505.1(e) and take appropriate action to ensure that NEPA objectives and procedures are achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both impacts and whether the action constrains reasonable alternative selection; take corrective action if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: prepare, make available, and issue FONSI or ROD
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare, make available for public review, and issue a FONSI or ROD as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete public availability and documentation steps required for final NEPA determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: EIS disclosure statement for contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that the draft and final EIS comply with 40 CFR 1506.5(c) and include a disclosure statement executed by any contractor (or subcontractor) under contract to prepare the EIS document, and that the disclosure appears as an appendix to the EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor disclosure regarding potential conflicts of interest or roles must be appended to the EIS as required by CEQ rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: compile and maintain the Administrative Record
rubrics_metrics.description: Compile, maintain, and produce the Administrative Record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain complete records to support NEPA decisions and for potential litigation or audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: periodic reporting on mitigation implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide periodic reports on implementation of Mitigation measures to NCPC and other Cooperating Parties consistent with a schedule established in the Environmental Document; all such reports shall be posted on NCPC's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a mitigation monitoring/reporting schedule in the Environmental Document and publicly post status updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: re-evaluate Environmental Documents five or more years old
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application that has yet to obtain final Commission approval, re-evaluate and update Environmental Documents that are five or more years old when (i) there are substantial changes to the proposed action relevant to environmental concerns; or (ii) there are significant new circumstances or information relevant to environmental concerns and bearing on the proposed action or its impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Older documents must be re-evaluated when the project or information has materially changed; this applies prior to final Commission approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency obligation: consult with NCPC on re-evaluation outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult with NCPC on the outcome of the re-evaluation; if NCPC disagrees with the Lead Agency's conclusion on the need to update, NCPC may prepare its own Environmental Document or decline to consider the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC has discretion to prepare its own document or stop processing if it disagrees with the Lead Agency's re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC as Lead: MOA requirement for most Non-Federal applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: When NCPC serves as Lead, require Non-Federal Agency applicants (other than the District of Columbia and the Maryland National Capital Parks and Planning Commission) to enter into a MOA with NCPC committing to provide all necessary assistance to facilitate NCPC's compliance with its NEPA obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOAs ensure Non-Federal applicants support NCPC's NEPA responsibilities; some local agencies are excepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC as Lead: MOA may be programmatic or project-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: The MOA may be prepared as a programmatic MOA addressing a uniform approach for all applications from a particular Non-Federal Agency applicant or address a specific application. The request for a project-specific MOA is made after a determination is made as to the inability to utilize a CATEX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic MOAs can streamline repeated interactions; project-specific MOAs are used when CATEX cannot be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC as Lead: MOA content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A MOA with a Non-Federal Agency shall specify roles and responsibilities; project information necessary to prepare the proper Environmental Document; project timelines and submission schedules; the submission of periodic reports on implementation of Mitigation measures; principal contacts and contact information; and a mechanism for resolving disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOAs must be detailed and cover technical, scheduling, reporting, and dispute resolution elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC as Lead: MOA publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon adoption of the MOA, NCPC shall publish the MOA in the Federal Register and post it on NCPC's Web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOAs are public documents and must be formally published and posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolving disputes over Lead Agency status
rubrics_metrics.description: In event of dispute with a Federal Agency applicant over Co-Lead status, parties shall use best efforts to cooperatively resolve disputes at working levels and, if necessary, elevate. If internal resolution fails, NCPC at its sole discretion may request CEQ's determination on which agency shall serve as Lead, prepare its own Environmental Document, or decline to take action on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process emphasizes negotiation; NCPC may seek CEQ intervention or proceed independently if unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating Agency role (NCPC when Federal applicant is Lead)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Federal Agency applicant serves as Lead, NCPC shall act as a Cooperating Agency and undertake duties described in 40 CFR 1501.6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC's legal obligations as a Cooperating Agency are tied to CEQ regulations; NCPC must follow cooperating-agency duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating Agency obligation: assist in MOA preparation and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist in the preparation of and sign a MOA with terms agreeable to NCPC if requested by the Lead Agency; MOA may be programmatic or application-specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperating agencies should negotiate MOA terms and may be party to programmatic or project-specific approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating Agency obligation: provide comprehensive, timely reviews and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in the NEPA process by providing comprehensive, timely reviews of and comments on key NEPA materials including Public Scoping notices; technical reports; documents (including responses to comments received from the public); the draft and final EA or EIS; and the Draft FONSI or ROD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, substantive review input from Cooperating Agencies is required on all major NEPA deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating Agency obligation: supply data and assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply available data, assessments, and other information that may be helpful in the preparation of the Environmental Document or the Administrative Record in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide existing technical information and assessments promptly to support NEPA analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating Agency obligation: independent evaluation and responsibility when sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Make an independent evaluation of the Federal Agency applicant's Environmental Document and take responsibility for the scope and contents of the EIS or EA when it is sufficient as required by 40 CFR 1506.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperating Agencies may assume responsibility for portions or the whole NEPA document if they independently evaluate and find it sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating Agency obligation: prepare or co-sign FONSI or ROD
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and, following Commission final approval of an application, sign a FONSI or ROD. Alternatively, if NCPC concurs with the contents of a Federal Agency's FONSI or ROD, NCPC may co-sign the Federal Agency's document following Commission final approval if co-signing is consistent with the Federal Agency's NEPA regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperating agencies can co-sign federal documents or prepare independent determinations consistent with agency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating Agency obligation: provide documentation for Administrative Record
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide documentation requested and needed by the Lead Agency for the Administrative Record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure documentation and supporting materials are provided to the Lead to support decision-making and recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating Agency contingency if excluded from meaningful participation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Federal Agency applicant fails to allow NCPC to participate meaningfully as a Cooperating Agency, parties shall use best efforts to resolve; may seek mediation; alternatively NCPC may prepare its own Environmental Document (stand-alone or supplement) or take no action on the underlying application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC has remedial options including producing its own analysis or declining to act when excluded from meaningful cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA compliance requirement: applicability (projects and master plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Agency applicants, and NCPC for Non-Federal Agency applications, shall comply with NEPA for: (1) projects requiring Commission approval; and (2) master plans requiring Commission action with future projects requiring subsequent Commission approval, provided the five-year and NEPA-satisfaction conditions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the categories of applications that must comply with NEPA under NCPC rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA submission timing: concept review scoping
rubrics_metrics.description: The NEPA Public Scoping process shall have been initiated by the applicant or NCPC before submission for concept review. Alternatively, if contemplating use of a CATEX, initiation of Public Scoping may be deferred until final decision on use of CATEX is made. Any NEPA information available at time of concept review shall be submitted to facilitate effective Commission concept review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoping should generally precede concept review; CATEX consideration can alter scoping timing but NEPA information available must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA submission timing: preliminary review requires Draft Environmental Document
rubrics_metrics.description: A Draft Environmental Document shall be issued or published before the applicant submits an application for preliminary review. NEPA information shall be provided to the Commission to facilitate meaningful preliminary review and comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a draft EA/EIS is available for Commission preliminary review so Commission can provide substantive direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA submission timing: final review requires FONSI or ROD
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of final approval submission, the determination (FONSI or ROD) resulting from the Environmental Document shall be submitted by the appropriate party (NCPC for Non-Federal applicants; Federal Agency applicant for Federal applicants) in a form consistent with NEPA regulations. NCPC may co-sign a Federal Agency's FONSI or ROD or prepare and sign its own independent document in accordance with §§601.16(a) or 601.25(a)-(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final determinations must accompany final applications; NCPC retains ability to co-sign or issue its own determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Circumstances: alternative arrangements and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Emergency Circumstances make necessary for the Commission to take action with significant environmental impact without observing these regulations, NCPC shall consult with CEQ about alternative arrangements and limit such arrangements to actions necessary to control immediate impacts; other actions remain subject to NEPA review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency actions are tightly constrained and require CEQ consultation; only immediate-impact control measures may be exempted temporarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviation for Emergency Circumstances when NCPC is Lead
rubrics_metrics.description: When NCPC is Lead, Emergency Circumstances exist, and an Extraordinary Circumstance precludes use of a CATEX, NCPC shall undertake one of specified actions (e.g., Executive Director prepares a concise, focused EA when necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special submission procedures apply in narrow emergency+extraordinary circumstances; NCPC must follow the prescribed alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-submission and dispute resolution at final review
rubrics_metrics.description: If Commission denies or requests changes at final review, the Federal Agency applicant shall proceed consistent with law and may revise the project responsive to Commission comments. Upon resubmission, the applicant shall submit revised Environmental Documents and FONSI/ROD if necessary. If NCPC and applicant disagree regarding need for revised documents, they shall work to resolve differences; final decision on need for revisions is made by the Commission's Executive Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must respond to Commission comments and may be required to revise NEPA documents; Executive Committee resolves disagreements about the need for re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of actions eligible for a Categorical Exclusion (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Categorical Exclusion is a type of action that does not individually or cumulatively have a significant effect on the human environment and has been found by NCPC to have no such effect. Actions that generally qualify exhibit: (1) minimal or no effect on the human environment; (2) no significant change to existing environmental conditions; (3) no significant cumulative environmental impacts; and (4) similarity to actions previously assessed in an EA concluding in a FONSI and monitored to confirm the FONSI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CATEX eligibility requires both low/no impacts and, where applicable, similarity to previously assessed actions with confirmed FONSIs; meet all listed characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to check for Extraordinary Circumstances before applying a CATEX
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying a CATEX listed in § 601.12, the Executive Director shall determine if a project or plan requires additional environmental review due to presence of Extraordinary Circumstances. If any listed Extraordinary Circumstances are present, the Executive Director shall not apply a CATEX and shall ensure an EA or EIS is prepared and made available to the Commission before action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Director must affirmatively screen for Extraordinary Circumstances; presence of any listed factor excludes CATEX use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary Circumstances categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Extraordinary Circumstances that preclude CATEX use include: (1) reasonable likelihood of significant impact on public health or safety; (2) likely significant impacts on sensitive resources unless avoided/minimized/mitigated (sensitive resources include federally listed threatened/endangered species or critical habitats; properties listed/eligible for National Register; areas with special designation such as National Historic Landmarks, floodplains, wetlands, National Parks; cultural, scientific or historic resources); (3) effects that are risky, highly uncertain, or unique; (4) likelihood of violating Executive Orders or laws protecting the environment; (5) likelihood of significantly increasing surface transportation congestion, disrupting mass transit, or interfering with pedestrian/bicycle movements; (6) likelihood of significantly degrading air quality or violating Clean Air Act standards; (7) likelihood of significantly impacting water quality, public water supply systems, or violating Clean Water Act or Safe Drinking Water Act standards; (8) likelihood of disproportionately high and adverse effects on low income and minority populations; (9) likelihood of degrading existing unsatisfactory environmental conditions; (10) likelihood of establishing a precedent for future actions or decisions in principle about future actions with potentially significant effects; (11) any other circumstance that makes the action sufficiently unique to warrant further analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are disqualifying factors for CATEX; include the enumerated resource and equity concerns, legal compliance, and uniqueness/uncertainty tests. If any apply, prepare EA/EIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Director documentation for CATEX decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director shall include in his/her Executive Director's Recommendation (EDR), or the documentation of a delegated action, the decision to apply a Categorical Exclusion including consideration of possible Extraordinary Circumstances or not apply a Categorical Exclusion because of Extraordinary Circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision to use CATEX must be documented in the EDR (or delegated action record) with explicit consideration of Extraordinary Circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC CATEX item: electrical distribution systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of the installation or restoration of onsite primary or secondary electrical distribution systems including minor solar panel arrays may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small-scale electrical distribution and minor solar arrays are normally CATEX-eligible unless Extraordinary Circumstances apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC CATEX item: minor site elements and replacement-in-kind utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of the installation or restoration of minor site elements (identification signs, sidewalks, patios, fences, curbs, retaining walls, landscaping, trail or stream improvements) and features including water distribution lines and sewer lines that involve work essentially replacement in kind may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine minor site work and in-kind utility replacements are typically CATEX-eligible; evaluate for Extraordinary Circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC CATEX item: minor building elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of the installation or restoration of minor building elements (windows, doors, roofs, building signs, rooftop equipment and green roofs) may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small-scale building repairs/replacements are normally CATEX-eligible unless they trigger Extraordinary Circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC CATEX item: adoption of Federal Element or broad policy/feasibility plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of a Federal Element of the Comprehensive Plan or amendment thereto or broad-based policy or feasibility plans prepared and adopted by the Commission in response to the Comprehensive Plan may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain planning or policy/adoption actions can be CATEX-eligible when they meet the general CATEX characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC CATEX item: communication antennae
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of the installation of communication antennae on Federal buildings and co-location of communication antennae on Federal property consistent with GSA Bulletin FMR D–242 may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antenna installations consistent with GSA guidance are listed CATEX actions; still check for Extraordinary Circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC CATEX item: new construction/building expansion limited criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of Federal and District government proposals for new construction, building expansion, or improvements to existing facilities may be categorically excluded when all of the following apply: (i) the new structure and proposed use are in compliance with local planning and zoning and any applicable District, state, or Federal requirements; (ii) the site and scale of construction are consistent with those of existing adjacent or nearby buildings; (iii) the proposed use will not substantially increase the number of motor vehicles in the vicinity; and (iv) there is little to no evidence of unresolved resource conflicts or community controversy related to environmental concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain small-scale or context-consistent construction/improvement projects can be CATEX-eligible if all four constraining criteria are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC CATEX item: transfers of jurisdiction under 40 U.S.C. 8124
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of transfers of jurisdiction pursuant to 40 U.S.C. 8124 that are not anticipated to result in changes in land-use and that have no potential for environmental impact may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictional transfers with no land-use changes or environmental impacts are CATEX-eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC CATEX item: minor modification to General Development Plan (Capper-Cramton lands)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of a minor modification to a General Development Plan applicable to lands acquired pursuant to the Capper-Cramton Act when non-significant environmental impacts are anticipated may be categorically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor plan modifications for Capper-Cramton lands are listed CATEX actions when impacts are non-significant.
